Opatow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Opatów, Poland

Not demolished. Opatów's Jewish cemetery, established no later than the 1630s, has one of the earliest documented grievances in this collection: in 1639, Jews accused a named Catholic clergyman, Canon Szymon Zelewski, of participating in the destruction of tombstones there. During the Holocaust, the cemetery became an execution site — about 300 people were shot and buried there, including several dozen members of the Judenrat and Jewish Order Service who had been kept alive to clean up the ghetto after its liquidation before being murdered themselves. Remarkably, the last known burial took place as late as September 5, 1945, following a raid on the house of Lejb Zilberberg — well after the war's end. The site was formally closed in 1956 and liquidated in 1962, after officials attributed its destruction to postwar tombstone theft; kindergartens, a community center, and a bandstand were later built there, and the rest became a park. In 1989, local enthusiasts established a lapidarium at the site, now listed on Poland's Register of Immovable Monuments.
